principle: A learner advances through demonstrated skills, not page completion. Skills are attached to source forms, language dependencies, and transfer tasks so a learner can use them beyond one memorized answer.

masteryScale.emerging: can make the move with support
masteryScale.secure: can make it in two familiar contexts
masteryScale.transfer: can make it in an unfamiliar source

skills.title: Orient to Hebrew on the page
skills.evidence: Distinguish a question, a speaker cue, and a cited teaching.

skills.title: Recognize question signals
skills.evidence: Identify a question word and predict the kind of answer it seeks.
skills.masteryCriteria: Predict the next move in an unfamiliar mini-source.

skills.title: Recognize source signals
skills.evidence: Identify when a verse or cited teaching is entering an argument.
skills.masteryCriteria: Explain what evidence is being introduced and why.

skills.title: Read high-frequency rabbinic phrases
skills.evidence: Recognize the argumentative job of a phrase before opening translation.
skills.masteryCriteria: Classify a phrase correctly in an unseen context.

skills.title: Map roles in a sentence
skills.evidence: Locate actor, action, object, and connector before translating.
skills.masteryCriteria: Map two short sentences with no word-for-word prompt.

skills.title: Use Aramaic question particles
skills.evidence: Label question, return, difficulty, and response moves in a short passage.
skills.masteryCriteria: Make a defensible first map before using translation to check it.

skills.title: Orient to a Mishnah
skills.evidence: State the case, category, or practical question before analyzing it.
skills.masteryCriteria: Separate the case from the later Gemara discussion.

skills.title: Identify a context question
skills.evidence: Explain what prior statement, source, or problem the Gemara is examining.
skills.masteryCriteria: Name the target of a question in an unfamiliar passage.

skills.title: Explain a proof text's role
skills.evidence: State whether a source supports, clarifies, challenges, or distinguishes a claim.
skills.masteryCriteria: Explain both the source and its argumentative role.

skills.title: Follow challenge and answer
skills.evidence: Mark an objection, the pressure it creates, and the response that follows.
skills.masteryCriteria: Map a challenge-and-answer sequence across two tractates.

skills.title: Read a short sugya independently
skills.evidence: Label each line's job in an unfamiliar source using translation only to verify.
skills.masteryCriteria: Produce a readable source map and explain one uncertainty responsibly.

skills.title: Identify a conceptual claim
skills.evidence: State what a source claims about God, human beings, values, or knowledge.
skills.masteryCriteria: Separate a source's claim from the learner's reaction.

skills.title: Define a key term
skills.evidence: Distinguish related concepts and explain why the distinction matters to an argument.
skills.masteryCriteria: Use the distinction in a second source.

skills.title: Compare interpretations
skills.evidence: State a shared source or question and identify where two readings diverge.
skills.masteryCriteria: Give each reading its strongest formulation before contrasting them.

skills.title: Apply an idea responsibly
skills.evidence: Explain how a source frames a question without mistaking philosophical reflection for halakhic ruling.
skills.masteryCriteria: Connect a concept to a new question while naming its limits.
